result:
`./compile.sh` reports success.

I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVParserAgentTest.java`, covering `CSVParser`'s documented contract: all six static `parse(...)` factories (including null-argument behavior per the javadoc's null-mapping/throws clauses), both deprecated constructors, `close()`/`isClosed()`, `nextRecord()`, `getRecords()` (including the empty-input and current-position-start cases, plus the documented `UncheckedIOException` wrapping via a `FailingReader` test double), `iterator()` (record order, closed-parser behavior, and the documented `IOException`→`IllegalStateException` conversion), `stream()`, `getCurrentLineNumber()`, `getFirstEndOfLine()`, `getHeaderMap()`/`getHeaderMapRaw()`/`getHeaderNames()` (including the documented copy-vs-underlying-reference distinction and read-only list), `getHeaderComment()`/`hasHeaderComment()`, `getTrailerComment()`/`hasTrailerComment()` (including the documented "only available after full processing" ordering), and `builder()`.

One constraint worth flagging: `CSVParser.Builder` extends a commons-io class (`AbstractStreamBuilder`) whose class file isn't in `lib/`. That made *every* `Builder` instance method — not just the origin setters — fail to compile, so I could only exercise the bare `CSVParser.builder()` factory call; the fluent setter/`get()` coverage I'd originally written had to be dropped in favor of equivalent coverage through the deprecated constructor (e.g. `recordNumber` offset behavior).
